guarantees.claim: For key_length_supplied equal to any of the enumerated values Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024, key_length is assigned the same value; for any other value, key_length is assigned Key_None.

formal.consequent: (key_length_supplied inside {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}) ? (key_length == key_length_supplied) : (key_length == Key_None)

formal_sketch.consequent: (key_length_supplied inside {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}) ? (key_length == key_length_supplied) : (key_length == Key_None)

guarantees.claim: Unsupported key_length_supplied values are silently mapped to Key_None.
guarantees.cond: key_length_supplied not in {Key_128, Key_256, Key_384, Key_512, Key_1024}

uncertain_points.claim: Downstream HMAC control logic (outside this chunk) is expected to block operation start and signal an error when key_length == Key_None, as per comments; verification needed to confirm the error detection and blocking path exists.
uncertain_points.cond: HMAC operation triggered with key_length == Key_None (i.e., unsupported key_length_supplied)
uncertain_points.risk: If blocking is missing, unsupported key lengths could allow HMAC to proceed with a default or unknown key, potentially breaking integrity or security properties.

security_implications: This block maps key length to an internal representation Key_None for unsupported values. If the downstream logic does not properly block HMAC operations when key_length == Key_None, the design may operate with an undefined key length, potentially reducing security strength or enabling incorrect HMAC computations. The mapping itself is safe, but the security property relies on external block/enforcement.
